summary: The note argues that vaccination is a lifelong commitment, not just a childhood matter, and walks through vaccines for infants, adolescents, adults, the elderly, and people with health conditions. It cites a series of experts and events from September 2023 to March 2024 on how vaccines work, measles resurgence, vaccine hesitancy, and public health campaigns. It closes with practical steps for staying on schedule and encouraging community vaccination.
one_line: Overview of why vaccination matters at every life stage, with expert comments on schedules, measles resurgence, hesitancy, and public health campaigns.
key_facts: Dr. Elaine Thorton, an epidemiology expert, explained on September 10, 2023 that vaccines train the immune system to recognize pathogens by introducing weakened or inactive components.
Paediatrician Dr. Jose Ramirez presented the recommended childhood vaccination timeline at a community workshop on October 5, 2023; the first vaccine is often against Hepatitis B.
Within their first year, children receive protection against tetanus, whooping cough, polio, and Hib, which causes meningitis.
The MMR vaccine has been the subject of unfounded controversy due to an infamous retracted study.
Family practitioner Dr. Sophia Liu said on November 18, 2023 that adolescents should get the HPV vaccine, which can prevent certain cancers, and a meningococcal vaccine.
The pertussis vaccine (Tdap) is especially recommended for pregnant women to protect newborns from whooping cough.
Adults over 50 are urged to receive shingles and pneumococcal vaccines, and annual flu shots are recommended for all ages.
Healthcare professional Mark Jennings said in a December 20, 2023 webinar that adults who missed childhood vaccines can catch up and that it is not too late.
Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, but its resurgence shows the danger of waning vaccination rates.
Immunologist Natalie Chen said on January 4, 2024 that measles outbreaks occurred in communities where vaccine coverage fell below the herd immunity threshold.
Behavioral psychologist Dr. Peter Hanson spoke on February 9, 2024 about listening to parental concerns and giving clear, evidence-based responses to counter vaccine hesitancy.

The campaign 'Vaccines for All: Every Age, Every Stage' began on September 15, 2023, and uses real stories of people protected by vaccines or harmed by preventable diseases, according to director Lara Gibson.
Pediatrician Dr. Omar Jefferson wrote in his March 1, 2024 clinic newsletter that staying on schedule is a form of preparedness that helps halt epidemics before they start.
People with chronic liver or heart disease, diabetes, or weakened immune systems may need additional vaccines, and travelers need destination-specific vaccines.
